questionsApplications.label: How can public organisations manage challenges that cross national borders?
Which development and migration strategies work, and under what governance conditions?

alternatives.concept: Closest feasible multidisciplinary approximation of MISOC, combining public administration, politics, international law, sociology, economics, organisation and social-research methods around international social challenges.
alternatives.labelRationale: The visible label was reviewed after completion of the 24-course curriculum and accurately presents this option as the closest feasible UCR response to Bachelor in Management of International Social Challenges, rather than as a narrower subfield.

alternatives.concept: A transnational governance route centred on global and European institutions, international law, migration, development, economics and technological change in public organisations.
basisLabels: How can public organisations manage challenges that cross national borders?

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the broad closest match, this route concentrates more heavily on transnational governance, international law, migration, development and economic/technological change, with less emphasis on climate-specific study.

notes.text: The Erasmus programme combines a structured Public Administration curriculum with international law, migration, development, research methods and a bachelor project. UCR can assemble strong multidisciplinary programmes around global governance and specific international challenges, but does not reproduce the same dedicated MISOC sequence or its named International Migration and Global Development Issues courses.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Re-audited under the substantial-curricular-correspondence rule. No available UCR row provides a sufficiently substantial counterpart without overstating partial or adjacent overlap.
Sociology I is most directly comparable to UCR Introduction to Sociology; this row was selected by semantic review after fixing the canonical UCR rows.
International law is most directly comparable to UCR Introduction to Public International Law; this row was selected by semantic review after fixing the canonical UCR rows.

Organisation & Management and UCR Psychology of Organizations & Leadership both address the functioning and management of organisations. Their framing differs, but the substantive organisational domain is sufficiently shared for row alignment.
Designing Social Research is most directly comparable to UCR Research Methods & Statistics; this row was selected by semantic review after fixing the canonical UCR rows.
Political Science is most directly comparable to UCR Foundations of Comparative Politics; this row was selected by semantic review after fixing the canonical UCR rows.
Economics, Welfare and Distribution is most directly comparable to UCR Introduction to Economics; this row was selected by semantic review after fixing the canonical UCR rows.

MISOC Skills serves academic and professional skill development, while UCR Personal & Professional Development develops core academic, communication, reflection and independent-learning skills. Their educational function substantially corresponds despite different programme framing.

Network Governance and UCR Governance of Sustainability both center governance as multi-actor collective decision-making involving public and non-public actors around public problems. UCR applies the governance framework to sustainability, but the primary governance content substantially corresponds.
